scope: Same checkpoint, prompt, seed; normal versus no_c on four reviewed paired videos, five frames each. no_c retains trained Wan LoRA and is not the official native model.

findings.VP004: no_c restores ruler markings and a visible fracture, although it starts broken and fails to show the requested fracture development. normal largely replaces this with a featureless straight translucent band. Normal PC4 versus no_c PC3 therefore cannot be interpreted as verified improved fracture physics; SA drops3 to2.
findings.VP009: no_c shows an actual suction-like lifting tool and a panel, albeit with incorrect handling. normal changes the scene into picture placement without the requested tool. Normal PC5 versus no_c PC3 accompanies SA3 to2 and omission of the requested interaction.
findings.VP015: normal includes an arm/oar and better represents the request than no_c, consistent with SA/PC4/4 versus3/3. Both modes still show a hull elevated above the water; normal does not resolve all contact/geometry failures.
findings.VP026: no_c has two recognizable people stretching material, although later body duplication/omission remains. normal emphasizes a long ribbon while people are lost. SA falls3 to2 with unchanged PC3.

conclusion: Physical conditioning has measurable effects and some useful cases, but several PC gains coexist with loss of requested process or detail. Overall paired score gains alone do not establish a robust genuine-physics improvement.
